subject: SUBTRACT statement
notes: Adjudicated 2026-08-31 with its ADD twin GR-14.9.2.4-4 (owner decision D-B; kb/Work PB156), which had left this row unverdicted. The SUBTRACT rule is the ADD rule one word apart — 'enough places shall be carried so as not to lose significant digits during execution' where ADD says 'not to lose any significant digits' (both cite.py --check verified; the 'verbatim twin' the design note claimed is very near but not literally verbatim). Same premise, same code path, same measurement: SUBTRACT 1.0E+0 FROM S (PIC 9(20) = 12345678901234567890) gave 12345678901234567168 at HEAD 6cd228b6 and gives 12345678901234567889 now. One rendering serves both statements, so the two rows cannot drift apart; pb156_float_literal_exact_native pins the ADD and SUBTRACT legs side by side for exactly that reason.
